# Trulana

> Your device is the API. A local-first private context server for AI tools.

Trulana turns your machine into a private context server. AI tools can request context about you — but your raw data never leaves your device. Every response is filtered on-device before it is returned.

## What it does

Instead of copying personal data into AI tools, Trulana inverts the model:

1. An app requests access via REST (localhost:8432) or MCP (stdio).
2. The user explicitly approves the agent; first-contact agents are pending until approved, and requested scopes can be narrowed before approval.
3. Trulana issues a short-lived, scoped access token (15-minute TTL, in-memory only, never persisted).
4. The app queries local context (e.g. "morning routine", "work colleagues").
5. The query is matched against an encrypted local vault.
6. The response passes through a 3-stage Auto-Redact Engine:
   - Stage 1: Regex filter (SSN, email, phone, credit card, IP)
   - Stage 2: NER processor (person names, locations, organizations)
   - Stage 3: Privacy filter (time generalization, amount generalization, age redaction)
7. Only the sanitized result is returned; raw context never leaves the device.
8. Every request is logged to an encrypted audit trail.

## Technical details

- Framework: Flutter (Dart 3.x) on macOS.
- Database: SQLite encrypted via sqflite_sqlcipher (AES-256).
- Key storage: flutter_secure_storage. The DB key is a symmetric AES key held as a generic Keychain item; it is not generated or operated on inside the Secure Enclave.
- REST API: shelf HTTP server bound to 127.0.0.1:8432 (loopback only; non-loopback rejected at the socket and in middleware).
- MCP: stdio JSON-RPC adapter triggered via TRULANA_MCP=1.
- Auth: Bearer tokens, 15-minute TTL, in-memory (do not survive restart).
- Scope enforcement: context.read required for /api/v1/context/query; monetize.write required for /api/v1/monetize/lease_offer.
- Rate limiting: 60 requests/minute per agent (REST only; MCP rate limiting not yet enforced).
- Shared service layer: REST and MCP are thin transports over the same AuthService / ContextQueryService, so token issuance, scope enforcement, redaction, and audit logging are identical across transports.

## MCP tools

- sovereign_request_access: Request a scoped access token. Requires app_id, app_name, scopes, intent.
- sovereign_query_context: Query personal context with a valid token. Response is automatically redacted.

## Privacy levels

- Standard: Regex + NER stripping only.
- Strict: Also generalizes times, currency amounts, ages.
- Paranoid: All of strict, plus a proper-noun catch-all and a noise disclaimer.

## Current limits

- MCP uses a local-process trust model (no cryptographic caller verification).
- MCP per-agent rate limiting is not yet enforced.
- NER uses keyword dictionaries (on-device LLM/SLM redaction is a future phase).
- Release signing and notarization are performed manually (CI builds an unsigned bundle).
- Audit log is encrypted-at-rest but not tamper-evident (no hash chain).
- macOS is the only public binary.

## Experimental (unreleased)

A Context-as-a-Service escrow layer (SHA-256 commitment + reveal, plus zero-width "watermark" provenance tagging) exists in the repository but is NOT part of the signed v1.2.1 binary and is not functional end-to-end (the commitment salt is not yet persisted between the lease-offer and settlement requests). It is a research preview and should not be represented as production.

## Release

macOS Desktop MVP, current release v1.2.1. Licensed under BUSL 1.1 (not MIT, not Apache); commercial production use requires a separate paid license from AdamsLocal LLC. No regulatory certifications (HIPAA, SOC 2, FedRAMP, GDPR, etc.) are claimed.
